title: Notes on iPhone, to iOS 6
lede: Apple’s iPhone notes app as a yellow ruled pad with a leather top and handwriting-style type, used until 2013.
summary: Lined, textured paper, a leather binding strip, and Marker Felt type. Apple, until 2013.
made: Until 2013 (Wikipedia); the Mac version followed in OS X Mountain Lion (2012)

evidence.note: Based on Wikipedia and NN/g. The NN/g article shows an image of the early iOS notepad, but it was not saved or measured here.

styles.note: A clear object metaphor: a paper notepad with ruled lines, textured paper, and a leather binding.

context: “Until 2013, both applications used a strongly skeuomorphic interface, with a lined, textured paper design; the Mountain Lion version placed this inside a leather folder.” Notes could use three fonts: Noteworthy, Marker Felt, and Helvetica. [Wikipedia: Notes (Apple)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notes_(Apple)).
NN/g: “This early iOS notepad design mimics a traditional paper notepad with textured lines and leather binding.” [NN/g: Skeuomorphism](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/skeuomorphism/).
interpretation: The handwriting face is part of the metaphor. The style record keeps it to places where the object would carry handwriting.
next: Inspect a large screenshot of iOS 6 Notes and record the paper color and rule spacing.

rights.statement: Apple software; copyrighted. No image is stored here.
